info.title: job-service
info.description:
Runs of jobs. A **job** is a named script in a repo's `jobs.toml`; a **run** is one execution of it, to completion at one commit, by a **runner** that claims it.

- A run is submitted `pending`, claimed and `running`, and ends `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled` with its exit code. It says what it was for when its submitter said.
- A run's log is read from any byte offset, while it runs and after: `GetRunLog` from where the last read ended, until `Run-State` says the run has ended.
- Runners call in and are never called: one registers with the registration token, then claims runs, appends to their logs and completes them with its own token, `<runner id>.<secret>`.

Submitters send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with the submitters' token, and may send `claimed-by`, recorded on a run they submit. `GetHealth` takes no token. Errors are `{code, message}`, the code an exception name for the HTTP status: `ValidationException` (400), `UnauthorizedException` (401), `AccessDeniedException` (403), `ResourceNotFoundException` (404), `ConflictException` (409), `PayloadTooLargeException` (413), `InvalidRangeException` (416), `InternalServerException` (500) and `ServiceUnavailableException` (503).

repo.description: `owner/name` on GitHub: the repo the routine is in.

dir.description: The routine's directory in that repo, holding the `jobs.toml` that names `job`: `/`-separated, no `.` or `..`.

memory.description: MiB the container may use, and the runner reserves for it. Null: `jobs.toml`'s, within the 1024 MiB a run without one is admitted with.

timeout.description: Seconds before the runner stops it and it fails. Null: `jobs.toml`'s.

kind.description: What asked for the run: an approval-service batch or change, a work-tracker item, or a worker.

For.description: What it was for; null when its submitter did not say.

timeout.description: Seconds before the runner stops it and it fails.

stall.description: Seconds without progress (output, CPU or network) before the runner ends it, failed as stalled; null when it never does.

RunsWith.description: What its runner runs it with: `limits`, else `jobs.toml`'s for the job, else its `[defaults]`. Null until its runner has read `jobs.toml`, and on a runner that does not say.

Where the job's steps live, when not in its own repo: `job` is read from `<dir>/jobs.toml` in `repo` at `commit`, and the run's own `repo` and `commit` are its target, the package checked out at `/work` beside the routine. Only a runner that says it `can` run a `routine` claims it.

host.description: The machine it must run on, as a runner's `hostId`: claimed only by that machine's runner, and only one that says it `can` run `host` runs, which runs it on the host itself, with the host's user services, if that host's config lets it. Null: any runner that fits.

can.description: What it can run beyond a job in its repo's own `jobs.toml`: `routine`, a run with a routine; `host`, a run naming its host, run on the host itself. A run needing one it does not say is left for another.

slots.description: Slots not taken by a run.

canceled.description: A cancel was asked for: stop the run and report it `canceled`.

exit.description: The run's exit code; null when it never ran or was killed.

reason.description: Why, when the state does not say: `timed out after 600s`, `image build failed`.

post.summary: Submit a run of a job: a named script in a repo at a commit
post.description: One run, stored `pending` until a runner whose labels and free memory fit claims it, with what it was for when `for` says. Nothing is checked against the repo here: a run of a job missing from `jobs.toml` at that commit fails on its runner, saying so in its log.

get.summary: Get a run's log from a byte offset
get.description: Send `Range: bytes=N-` to read from offset N; without it, from 0. Answers 206 with `Content-Range: bytes N-M/size` and at most 1 MiB, or an empty body when N is the log's size, so a follower polls from where it got to. `Run-State` says the run's state, so it knows when to stop.

206.description: The log from N, up to 1 MiB.

schema.description: `bytes N-M/size` for the bytes sent, or `bytes */size` when there are none: `size` is the log's length so far.

content-range.description: `bytes N-M/size` for the bytes sent, or `bytes */size` when there are none: `size` is the log's length so far.

schema.description: The run's state: once it has ended and the log is read to `size`, there is no more.

run-state.description: The run's state: once it has ended and the log is read to `size`, there is no more.

patch.summary: Append to the log of a run in progress, and renew its lease
patch.description: The body is the bytes, `Content-Range: bytes S-E/*` where S is the log's current size and E = S + length - 1. An empty body without `Content-Range` only renews the lease. 416 for any other S, with the size to resend from. At most 256 KiB per append and 64 MiB per run (413). The reply says whether a cancel was asked for.
